Let’s dive into Chapter 3: Diagnosing the Real Challenge.
You know, at the heart of any truly effective strategy, there’s always a sharp, honest diagnosis of the situation. But here’s the thing—this step gets skipped or rushed way too often. Why does it matter so much? Well, without really understanding the true challenge, even the hardest work can end up missing the mark entirely.
Diagnosis isn’t just about gathering piles of data or listing every problem you see. It’s about making sense of the chaos, spotting patterns, and homing in on what actually matters. Imagine a doctor facing a patient with a bunch of symptoms. The goal isn’t just to treat everything at once—it’s to dig deep and find the root cause. That’s exactly what a good strategist does. They sift through all the noise, look for the signal, and define what’s really at the core.
So, what does a great diagnosis actually do? Let me break it down for you.
Simplifies Complexity. It cuts through the clutter and puts the spotlight on the factors that count. That doesn’t mean you ignore the details—it just means you find the thread that connects it all.
Identifies Leverage Points. It shows you where a small change could make a huge difference. These are the hidden spots where your effort can really pay off.
Shapes the Guiding Policy. Once you know what the real challenge is, you can build a plan that actually addresses it. The diagnosis lays the foundation for every step that follows.
Diagnosing well often means questioning what everyone thinks they already know. Organizations can get stuck telling themselves stories—maybe blaming outside forces, or assuming that if they just work harder, things will improve. But a smart diagnosis digs deeper and asks the tough questions—could our own choices or structures be part of the issue?
Here’s a real-world example: Think about a retail chain that’s seeing fewer people walk through the door. It’s easy to blame online shopping. But what if there’s more to it? Maybe the neighborhoods around the stores are changing. Or maybe the in-store experience just isn’t exciting anymore. By looking below the surface, the business can spot the real challenge—and avoid wasting money on the wrong fixes.
And remember, diagnosis isn’t something you do once and forget about. As the world changes, so does the nature of the challenge. That means you have to keep paying attention, and be willing to update your understanding. Especially in fast-moving industries, what was true last year might not help you today.
So, what’s a practical way to tackle diagnosis?
Start by gathering information—pull in data from inside and outside your organization. Then, look for patterns; what trends or oddities jump out? Keep asking “why?” over and over, to get beneath the surface and find the real root causes. Challenge your assumptions—do they really stand up to the facts? And finally, focus on what matters. Boil everything down to a clear, honest statement about what the core challenge really is.
I won’t sugarcoat it—this process isn’t always easy. It can uncover weaknesses and spark tough conversations. But if you want your strategy to be grounded in reality, it’s absolutely essential.
So, here’s the key takeaway: A well-crafted diagnosis doesn’t just list problems. It frames the challenge in a way that makes action possible. It gives you—and your whole organization—a lens for seeing what’s really going on, and deciding where to focus your efforts for the biggest impact.
